reason: The unheated bank margin is the visible location for taking a reference core beyond the melted cavity.
expectation: The drill should extract an unmelted reference core from the bank.

effect: The sealed source core is ready to store before the farther expedition.
reaction: The brown flakes preserved in place make the reference core intriguing.
reason: The laboratory core freezer is the obvious place to store the sealed core.
expectation: The core will be stored frozen for later examination.

effect: The source core is stored separately from the original membrane, completing the chapter and leaving both samples behind for the farther expedition.
reaction: The separate storage is a reassuring detail, though the expedition remains unresolved.

mostWorthwhile.text: Taking the unheated reference core was most worthwhile: the flakes remained in place in the ice, giving the investigation a more useful comparison with material from the melted well.

leastWorthwhile.text: Storing the core was a necessary but straightforward follow-up, with little decision-making beyond choosing the freezer.

surprise.text: The brown flakes appeared in the unmelted ice too, rather than only in material collected from the strainer.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: drilling beyond the heated cavity and freezing the sealed core both had clear purposes.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see what the farther samples reveal and whether the investigation can explain the segmented body; this chapter set up that question rather than resolving it.
